statement: Given a vector space V over a field K, the linear span (or linear hull) of a set S of vectors (not necessarily finite), denoted span(S) or ⟨S⟩, is defined as the intersection of all linear subspaces of V that contain S. Equivalently, it is the smallest subspace of V containing S and the set of all finite linear combinations of elements of S: span(S) = {λ_1 v_1 + λ_2 v_2 + ⋯ + λ_n v_n ∣ n ∈ ℕ, v_1, …, v_n ∈ S, λ_1, …, λ_n ∈ K}.

symbols.meaning: subset of vectors whose span is formed
number of terms in a finite linear combination

properties.property: span(S) is the smallest (for set inclusion) linear subspace of V containing S, and equals the intersection of all subspaces of V containing S.
properties.why: Any subspace containing S must be closed under addition and scalar multiplication and thus must contain all finite linear combinations of elements of S.
When S is empty, n = 0 and the expression reduces to the empty sum which by convention evaluates to the zero vector 0.

properties.property: When S = {v_1, …, v_n} is finite, span(S) = {λ_1 v_1 + ⋯ + λ_n v_n ∣ λ_1, …, λ_n ∈ K}.
properties.why: All finite linear combinations of elements from a finite set can be written with the entire set by allowing coefficients in K.

properties.property: Every spanning set S of a vector space V contains at least as many elements as any linearly independent set of vectors from V.
properties.why: Linearly independent vectors adjoined to a spanning set allow successive replacement of vectors while preserving the spanning property without contradiction.

properties.property: Any spanning set of a finite-dimensional vector space V can be reduced to a basis for V by discarding linearly dependent vectors.
properties.why: Removing linearly dependent vectors does not reduce the span, leaving a minimal spanning set.

assumptions.assumption: V is a vector space over a field of scalars K.
assumptions.breaks_when: The ambient structure lacks field scalar multiplication (e.g., modules over arbitrary rings where linear combinations are module sums).

assumptions.assumption: Linear combinations are restricted to finite sums of vectors.
assumptions.breaks_when: Infinite sums are attempted without an ambient topological or normed vector space structure providing convergence.

failure_modes.signature: span(S) ⊊ V (vectors in V cannot be represented as linear combinations of S).
failure_modes.cause: The set S does not contain vectors with non-zero components along all directions of V (e.g., {(1,0,0), (0,1,0), (1,1,0)} spans only vectors with third component zero in ℝ³).

failure_modes.signature: Representations of vectors as linear combinations of S are non-unique.
failure_modes.cause: The spanning set contains linearly dependent vectors, meaning it spans the space but fails to be a basis.
Overlooking the standard convention that an empty linear combination evaluates to the zero vector 0.
